summary: This regulation sets the rules for how the board of directors of a listed company must be put together and run. It covers who must be on the board, how often they must meet, and what duties they must handle. It ensures companies have proper balance, diverse members, and regular reviews.
points: The board of directors must have an optimum mix of executive and non-executive directors, including at least one woman director.
At least half of the board must consist of non-executive directors.
The board of directors must meet at least four times a financial year, with no more than one hundred and twenty days between meetings.
The board must periodically review compliance reports for all laws applicable to the listed entity.
The board must lay down a code of conduct for all its members and senior management.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is a listed company preparing for its annual board structuring. The board ensures that at least half of its members are non-executive directors and includes at least one woman director as required. To meet operational rules, the directors schedule their meetings so that there is a maximum time gap of one hundred and twenty days between any two consecutive gatherings. Furthermore, the board lays down a formal code of conduct for all members and senior management, ensuring that everyone follows the correct governance standards.

terms.meaning: A member of the board of directors who is also part of the daily management and operations of the company.
A member of the board of directors who is not involved in the day-to-day running of the company.
A non-executive board member who does not have any material or pecuniary relationship with the company, its promoters, or its management.
The minimum number of members that must be present at a meeting to make the proceedings valid.

watch: People often confuse non-executive directors with independent directors, but all independent directors are non-executive while not all non-executive directors are independent.
